items.stem: Under the IFRS 15 five-step model, when is revenue recognised?

options.text: As each performance obligation is satisfied by transferring control to the customer
options.rationale: Correct: revenue is recognised when control of the promised good or service transfers.

options.text: When the invoice is issued, regardless of delivery
options.rationale: Invoicing does not determine recognition; transfer of control does.
IFRS 15 is not a cash-basis model.

options.text: Evenly over the entity's financial year
options.rationale: Timing follows satisfaction of obligations, not the calendar.

items.explanation: Correct: revenue is recognised when control of the promised good or service transfers.

items.stem: Which TWO conditions generally support recognising a provision under IAS 37? (Select TWO)

options.text: A present obligation exists from a past event
options.rationale: Correct: a provision requires a present obligation arising from a past event.

options.text: An outflow of resources is probable and can be reliably estimated
options.rationale: Correct: probable outflow and a reliable estimate are required.

options.text: The obligation is merely possible and not estimable
options.rationale: That is a contingent liability, disclosed not provided.

options.text: Management simply prefers to smooth profits
options.rationale: Provisions cannot be used to smooth earnings.

items.explanation: Correct: a provision requires a present obligation arising from a past event.

items.stem: Under IAS 1, how should an asset expected to be realised within the normal operating cycle be classified?

options.rationale: Correct: assets realised within the operating cycle or 12 months are current.
Only items outside the cycle/12 months are non-current.
It is an asset, not equity.
Classification concerns the balance sheet, not revenue.

items.explanation: Correct: assets realised within the operating cycle or 12 months are current.
